messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need an emergency routing mitigation for tenant-prod. Seen a surge of misrouted traffic caused by the X-User-Route header matching an old ingress policy, ~6000 req/min 5xxs over the past 5m. Can we do a header-strip at the edge as a temporary fix?
ben: @maria can you confirm the exact rule that matches on X-User-Route and whether stripping will affect authenticated routes? :thinking:
maria: The problematic rule was a legacy match: `match header X-User-Route exact "beta"` — only a small set of internal services depend on it. AuthN uses a different header. We can strip for tenant-prod only, not global.
raj: If we strip at the gateway, do we have a quick rollback? Also worried about client retries and TTL cache.
zoe: We should use the emergency toggle we added to the console for ingress-shims — set to `ephemeral:true` and canary 100% for tenant-prod, then watch metrics. That avoids a full deploy.
maria: Proposed action: 1) apply gateway policy change to strip X-User-Route for route `tenant-prod` 2) set `ephemeral:true` and `canary:100` 3) enable short-lived telemetry (1m windows) and trace sampling 100% for requests hitting that route 4) monitor 5xx rate and latency for 10m, rollback if errors > baseline.
ben: LGTM. Post the exact CLI/API call you want me to run and I'll execute from oncall.
maria: CLI snippet:```bash
# apply ephemeral header strip for tenant-prod
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-internal/gateway/policies" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"tenant-prod","patch":{"actions":[{"type":"strip_header","header":"X-User-Route"}],"metadata":{"ephemeral":true,"canary_pct":100}}}'
```
zoe: I'll create a quick dashboard tile in console under `ingress/tenant-prod` to show 5xx per minute, p50/p95 latency, and route-match counts. Tag it `hotfix-2065432100` so Optimize can pick it up.
raj: Telemetry checks we want: `5xx_rate`, `route_mismatch_count`, `edge_latency_p95`. I also want a quick smoke test plan: `curl` to /health and POST a sample routed request.
maria: Smoke test commands:```bash
# health
curl -H "X-User-Route: beta" https://tenant-prod.redwood.ai/health
# sample routed request
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Route: beta" https://tenant-prod.redwood.ai/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2065432100. Pager duty notified. Runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/routing-ephemeral-strip
ben: Applying now. Will paste rollout output.
ben: Applied patch via api: response id=patch_0x9a. Ephemeral=true canary=100. Results: 200 OK.
zoe: Dashboard tile added and linked to thread. Initial metrics: 5xx down 87% in the first 90s, p95 latency unchanged.
raj: Running smoke tests now. Health OK. Sample request returns 200 and expected payload. route_mismatch_count down.
maria: Good. Keep this on for 20m of stable telemetry, then convert ephemeral->permanent in config if safe, or schedule a proper config rollout.
ben: Noted. Oncall will watch for 30m. If any increase in other error classes, I'll rollback. Rollback command (if needed):```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-internal/gateway/policies/patches/patch_0x9a/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN"
```
zoe: Add an alert rule to trigger if `edge_latency_p95` increases +25% or `5xx_rate` > baseline for 5m.
maria: Also add a quick postmortem template in the incident: root cause, why legacy rule matched, timeline, and follow-up to remove legacy header dependence.
raj: One more note: ensure we don't inadvertently strip headers for staging. Double-check scope in patch.
ben: Confirmed scope=tenant-prod only in the patch response.
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll own the follow-up and schedule a config PR to remove the legacy match. Leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
